# Gridland's look

Decided 2026-10-06.

## Direction: detailed pixel art, generated by code

- **The simulation stays on the tile grid.** That's what keeps it cheap, repeatable from a seed, and summarisable
  for time away (docs/PLAYER.md). Only the presentation changes.
- **Detailed pixel art**, at roughly 16–32 px per tile (Stardew / Eastward level), replacing today's 8 px tiles
  and 6 px bots. The goal is legibility: you should recognise a bot you've followed for days, see a child grow
  into an elder, and spot family resemblance.
- **Every sprite is generated by code. No hand-drawn or bought assets.** A character is built from layers chosen
  by the sim:

  | Layer | Driven by |
  |---|---|
  | body size and shape | age stage (child, adult, elder) |
  | skin, hair, eye colour | inherited from the parents |
  | clothing colour and style | traits and job |
  | held item, tool | `carrying`, `has_tool` |
  | posture, expression | mood, stress, goal |

  Inheritance then becomes visible for free, and new systems add a layer rule instead of new artwork.
- Tiles get the same treatment: variants from a per-tile hash (as today, but with more detail), plus
  edge-aware transitions (shorelines, path edges, field borders).

## Consequences

- **Rendering moves off the CPU pixel buffer.** Today Rust writes every pixel of a 512×512 image each frame. At
  16–32 px per tile and with a bigger, zoomable world, that doesn't scale. Likely shape: Rust (or JS) draws sprites
  **once** into atlases (a bot's sprite is redrawn only when its look changes); the page draws them with a GPU or
  Canvas2D `drawImage` path; lighting becomes a scaled-up multiply layer. Canvas2D vs PixiJS (used in Pavement) is
  decided by a spike, not up front.
- The 8 px night lighting in `render.rs` (2026-10-06) is a stopgap and moves to the new renderer.
- UI overlays (bubbles, selection) are already positioned in world coordinates; keep it that way
  (see the world-size note in memory: UI must not be tied to world size).

## Tile size: 32 px (decided 2026-10-06)

Chosen after the sprite test (`spikes/sprites/`, commit 869e7cf). At 32 px characters have readable faces (eyes, brows,
expressions, wrinkles) and family resemblance shows; at 16 px a face is three pixels. Consequences:
- A 64×64 world is 2,048 px wide at 1×, so the camera (pan, zoom out below 1×, follow a bot) is required, not optional.
  The default view is zoomed out, and you zoom in to read faces.
- Terrain and objects must be drawn with real 32 px detail. The spike only doubled its 16 px shapes.
- Character geometry starts from the spike's 32 px `GEOM` (child, adult, elder) and layer rules.

## The spike (done)

Built and reviewed: `spikes/sprites/` draws families, jobs, moods and a village corner at both sizes. The renderer
choice (Canvas2D vs PixiJS) is still open.
